investigate.rootCauseOneLine: plugins/github/server.ts checkAuth() maps every `gh auth status` failure (a network probe: outage, locked keychain, 10 s timeout) to NeedsConfigurationError, which the load-time probe reports via bb.status.needsConfiguration and the sync service throws out of start(); the plugin runtime then stops the service "until reload" and keeps needs-configuration until the next load, the plugin API has no way to clear it, and the app skips the frontend bundle of non-running plugins, so nothing ever re-runs gh and the "run gh auth login" hint cannot help.
investigate.proposedFix: Plugin-only change in plugins/github/server.ts (prototype diff at /tmp/bb-reports/issues/1758/repro/proposed-fix.diff, applied in the worktree; makes the 4-test repro file pass and keeps bb-plugin-github typecheck/tests green): (1) checkAuth() throws NeedsConfigurationError only when gh is missing or holds no credentials at all, using the network-free `gh auth token` to tell "not logged in" from "logged in but the API probe failed"; other failures become a plain Error carrying gh's stderr. (2) The sync service catches non-configuration errors inside its loop and retries with backoff (30 s doubling to the 5-min interval) instead of throwing out of start(). (3) The status RPC re-runs checkAuth() when the last probe failed so the panel/CLI reflect current state. (4) Load-time only calls bb.status.needsConfiguration for the two genuine configuration cases and logs transient failures. Follow-ups: reword the panel banner in app.tsx, make resolveGh() distinguish ENOENT from timeout, and optionally add an experimental_ degraded/clear status API to the plugin runtime so bb plugin list can show a transient gh problem.
investigate.caveats: Reproduced on Linux with gh 2.96.0 (issue reports macOS 26 / gh 2.95.0 / bb 0.38.0); the macOS locked-keychain trigger is unverified here but takes the identical code path (any non-zero exit of `gh auth status`). investigate.rootCauseOneLine: timelineWindowEventBudget bounds synchronous timeline builds by a fixed event count justified by a one-host "0.06ms/event" figure, but build cost is CPU- and payload-byte-dependent (SQLite read + JSON.parse ~80%), so on slow hosts a full 1500-event window blocks the event loop far longer than the ~100ms the constant promises; the existing 4 MiB byte cut is not operator-tunable and never engages for latency.

prReviews.topFinding: Docs-only; bakes one VPS's unverifiable and selection-biased numbers (derived only from >=150ms slow-build log lines) into the shared feature-flags.ts JSDoc, and the configuration.md recipe omits that the log samples only the slow tail and that a whole finished turn is always returned even above the budget; does not touch the real lever (the existing byte-based window cut).

investigate.proposedFix: Promote the existing THREAD_TIMELINE_EVENT_DATA_BYTE_LIMIT (4 MiB, applyTimelineWindowByteBudget / findStoredTimelineWindowByteBudgetFloor) to a feature flag timelineWindowByteBudget (BB_FF_TIMELINE_WINDOW_BYTE_BUDGET) threaded like eventBudget, default ~1.5 MiB with 4 MiB kept as the memory clamp; document both knobs (configuration.md, guide template, bb-cli skill) and reword the source comment to say the count is a hardware/payload-dependent proxy. Avoid runtime calibration unless the timeline cache and latest-rows keys also include the effective budget. Structural fix (out of scope): incremental projection or moving the build off the event loop.
investigate.caveats: Could not measure on the reporter's 4-core VPS; hardware dependence was demonstrated by CPU-throttling the same test (~4x cost, 124.5ms > 100ms for a full window) rather than on real slow hardware. On this Ryzen 7 workstation the constant is conservative (0.024 ms/event). The reporter's 0.479 ms/event p50 is a slow-tail estimate because the log line only fires for builds >= 150ms. Nothing on origin/main after the base commit changes this code. No dev instance or provider turns were needed.

The sustained-rebuild mechanism is real but its magnitude is overstated.

investigate.rootCauseOneLine: Node already sizes the V8 heap from min(RAM, cgroup memory.max/memory.high) via uv_get_constrained_memory; the reporter's 1728 MB is exactly the value derived from MemoryHigh=3G (a 4.9 GiB host with no cgroup gives 2240 MB), so the "cgroup ignored" premise is false; the residual real gap is that every co-located Node process (server, daemon, bridges) gets ~half the cgroup and there is no per-process heap knob because NODE_OPTIONS is inherited by all of them.

prReviews.topFinding: resolveServerNodeFlags reads process.env, so `bb-app env set BB_SERVER_MAX_OLD_SPACE_MB` (which the PR's docs row advertises) is silently ignored (verified live: server spawned without the flag while its env has the value); also the validation error is swallowed by `bb-app start` and reported as 'health check timed out', and the docs/comment restate the false 'Node ignores cgroup limits' premise.

investigate.proposedFix: Do not implement the issue as filed (deriving --max-old-space-size from memory.max re-implements Node's default and yields the same 1728 MB); retitle to the real gap: no way to cap the server heap independently of daemon/bridges in a shared cgroup. If a knob is wanted, read it from the launcher's resolved env (runtime.serverEnv), validate at option-resolution time so bb-app start surfaces the error, apply at both server spawn sites, document without the wrong premise, add tests. Optionally a co-location-aware default (server gets ~40% of min(memory.high, memory.max) when a cgroup limit is detected, overridable), and separately heap-snapshot the server's ~625 MB trough to see whether it is retained live state.
investigate.caveats: Reporter's RSS/OOM measurements are host-specific and unverifiable here; NODE_OPTIONS propagation to bridge processes was verified by code and the existing process-utils unit test, not by spawning a live provider turn; the native claude binary on this machine ignores NODE_OPTIONS (npm/Node installs would not). One `bb-app env set` invocation during PR testing lacked BB_SERVER_PORT and triggered a harmless config reload on the machine's real bb server on :38886 (no data changed). Test cgroup runs used systemd-run --user --scope on this host's node 24.18 (reporter has 24.19; same libuv/Node logic).

investigate.rootCauseOneLine: Archiving the last live thread of a managed worktree retires the environment and, after the 5-minute grace window (PR #1016), the daemon runs `git worktree remove --force` and the environment becomes the terminal `destroyed` state; from there the app hides Unarchive/composer/handoff, unarchive only clears archivedAt (thread becomes live-but-unwritable, send -> 409 thread_environment_unavailable), fork is rejected, and no route/CLI can attach a new workspace to the thread — the deferred "continue from destroyed environment" path was never built.
investigate.proposedFix: Server: add POST /threads/:id/restore-environment for threads whose managed-worktree environment is `destroyed` — create a new managed-worktree environment on the same host with baseBranch = old environment's branchName (the logic resolveForkEnvironment already has), updateThread({environmentId}) (DB layer supports it, emits environment-changed), let normal provisioning build the worktree, verify/fallback provider session resume with the new cwd. App/CLI/SDK: in the environment-gone banner add "Restore workspace from branch <b>" and "Continue in new thread" (handoff without reuseEnvironmentId), same in the "..." menu instead of a bare Unarchive that yields a zombie; add `bb thread restore-environment`; show the 5-minute deadline in the archived banner and rename "Environment archived" to "Workspace deleted". Cheap intermediate: allow fork (isolated mode) from a destroyed environment that still has branchName and expose it in the banner. investigate.rootCauseOneLine: Pi extension-triggered turns (pi.sendMessage custom message with triggerTurn) emit role:"custom" message_start/message_end envelopes that bb's Pi translator classifies as provider/unhandled, and Pi's agent_end.messages contains that custom entry with string content which bb's piConversationMessageSchema (array-only) rejects, so agent_end becomes provider/unhandled and no turn/completed is ever emitted — the extension-started turn has no pi/prompt/settled fallback, so the thread stays 'Working…' forever with no input shown.

prReviews.topFinding: The string-content schema widening (the #1663 commit) correctly unsticks the turn, but the new item/completed userMessage projection is rendered by nothing in thread-view/app/CLI (verified live: bb thread log shows two consecutive 'ok' rows with no input), so 'process event is visible as turn input' is unmet; the 'no text response' warning path is dead because real Pi emits agent_start before the custom message_start (all new tests use the reversed order; probe test fails on the PR), and the fix keys on the third-party literal customType 'ad-process:notification' instead of role:'custom' generally.

investigate.proposedFix: (1) Widen piConversationMessageSchema.content to z.union([z.string(), z.array(block)]) (as in #1663) — sufficient to emit turn/completed for extension-triggered turns; also JSON-round-trip raw events in toProviderRawEvent so unhandled payloads are not replaced by the serialization-error stub. (2) Handle message_start/message_end with role:'custom' generically in the Pi translator (project display:true custom messages as turn input when a bb turn is open, mark the rest as noise in visibility.ts) rather than matching customType 'ad-process:notification'. (3) Add a rendering path for provider-originated input: either project item/completed userMessage in @bb/thread-view (build-event-projection.ts + timeline/CLI formatters + snapshot test) as a user row with a non-user initiator, or emit an operation-style event that already renders. Tests must use the real order agent_start → message_start(custom). No HOST_DAEMON_PROTOCOL_VERSION bump needed as ThreadEvent shapes are unchanged. Follow-up: idle provider-session reaping (30 min) disposes Pi sessions together with extension-owned background processes, which is a real 'never wakes' path.
investigate.caveats: @aliou/pi-processes itself was not installed; the live repro uses a 30-line stand-in Pi extension sending the identical message shape (copied from pi-processes 0.10.9 source) via pi.sendMessage(..., {triggerTurn:true, deliverAs:'steer'}), run in a trusted scratch project via PI_CODING_AGENT_DIR pointing at a copy of ~/.pi/agent (bb's bridge has no Pi trust prompt, so project extensions are otherwise skipped silently). investigate.rootCauseOneLine: bb keeps one long-lived `claude` CLI process per thread (never recycled after a rate-limit/auth failure), and that process memoizes the OAuth token it loaded at startup, only invalidating it when the mtime of ~/.claude/.credentials.json changes or via a 30 s (stale-on-failure) Keychain cache on macOS; a login the probe cannot see stays pinned until a new process (server restart / thread stop) is spawned.
investigate.proposedFix: In plugins/provider-claude-code/src/bridge/bridge.ts, when a turn's SDK result is_error with category rate-limit/unauthorized/billing (error-info.ts), flag the ThreadSession recycle-on-next-input and have getWritableThreadSession treat it like streamEnded: settle, emitSessionReplacement, and start(providerThreadId) a fresh SDK session (existing replaceEndedThreadSession path). The new claude process reads credentials at startup so a login done in between applies on retry; conversation survives via SDK resume; no wire change (no protocol bump). Interim workaround: `bb thread stop <id>` on the idle thread releases the runtime so the next message spawns a fresh process (verified).
investigate.caveats: Plain Linux flow (claude login rewrites .credentials.json) does NOT reproduce with Claude Code 2.1.233/2.1.234: the CLI notices the mtime change and reloads on the next request. The pinned-token behaviour was reproduced deterministically only when the store changes without an mtime change (Linux analog of a macOS Keychain login next to a leftover plaintext file, or a failed/timed-out Keychain re-read). macOS could not be run here; the Keychain-cache analysis comes from reading the shipped darwin binaries' embedded JS. Reporter's OS/CLI version unknown; suggested check: `ls -la ~/.claude/.credentials.json` on their Mac and CLI debug logs for "[keychain] read failed; serving stale cache".

investigate.proposedFix: Tier 1: in plugins/automations/src/cli.ts print the resolved source path and the stored copy path on create/update with a note that it is a snapshot refreshed only by `update --script-file`; expose storedScriptPath in AutomationResponse so `show`/UI display it; resolve --script-file against ctx.cwd (plugin CLI runs server-side, so the documented `./watch.sh` currently ENOENTs); document copy semantics in the automations SKILL.md, guide template, and bb-cli skill. investigate.rootCauseOneLine: bb-app's waitForHealth() accepts any 200 from /health on the configured port (a constant {ok:true}) with no identity check, so a foreign bb server on the same port satisfies the probe on the first poll before the launcher's own server child dies with EADDRINUSE; the launcher then mints an enroll key from that foreign server and its daemon persists the resulting host key into the wrong data dir (before binding its own port), which the correct server later rejects with 401/INVALID_API_KEY.
investigate.proposedFix: Make the launcher's server readiness probe prove identity, not liveness: generate a per-launch id (e.g. BB_SERVER_LAUNCH_ID=randomUUID()) in startFullStackServerProcess, pass it to the server child env, have the server echo it on /health (or a loopback-only /internal/launch-identity), and have waitForHealth accept only a 200 whose id matches (mirroring waitForHostDaemonStatus, which already checks hostId/serverUrl). A foreign server then never satisfies the probe, the child's EADDRINUSE exit surfaces as 'Process exited before becoming healthy', and maybeAddAutoJoinEnv/enrollment is never reached. Launcher-to-server only; no HOST_DAEMON_PROTOCOL_VERSION bump. Also: server should log 'Server listening' only on the listening event and turn EADDRINUSE into a bb-authored fatal message; superviseFullStackProcesses should stop after N consecutive exit-before-listen restarts instead of looping '✓ Server restarted' forever; daemon's fatal 401/403 message can hint that <dataDir>/auth.json is unknown to <serverUrl> and can be removed to re-enroll (do not auto-delete).

INVALID_API_KEY is a Better Auth internal server log line, not a bb message. investigate.rootCauseOneLine: ThreadDetailView mounts ~12-15 independent per-thread queries with nothing deferred, and useEnvironmentWorkStatus (staleTime 0, refetchOnMount "always") / useEnvironmentPullRequest (refetchOnMount, refetchOnWindowFocus "always") drive uncached server->daemon git and `gh pr view` probes (70-260 ms git, 1.1-1.6 s GitHub API) on every open, forming a 3-tier waterfall.
investigate.proposedFix: (1) Cache workspace.status in the host daemon per environment, invalidated by the existing WatchManager work-status-changed/git-refs-changed events and daemon-owned mutations, with a short TTL and coalescing (daemon-internal, no protocol bump). (2) Stop probing GitHub per open: useEnvironmentPullRequest -> refetchOnMount false, drop refetchOnWindowFocus "always", refresh on git-refs-changed only, and memoize the last gh pr view result per branch in the daemon. (3) Gate status/PR queries, thread-storage listing, tabs, and fork/parent child-thread lists on the surface that renders them being open (none visible on mobile first paint). (4) Fix the double status refetch per open. Do not add an aggregate bootstrap endpoint (rejected history in #335/#1470/#1481).
investigate.caveats: Measured in dev mode (Vite, StrictMode double-fires, HTTP/1.1 proxy) with a 1-message thread; distinct-URL counts (12-15) are slightly below the issue's ~19 and depend on the thread's tabs/panels. Mobile RTT was emulated via CDP in headless Chromium, not a real iPhone; the reporter's 3-15 s taps over a Cloudflare tunnel were not reproduced on-device. The pull-request timing used a scratch repo pointed at github.com/get-bb/bb (gh returns absent after a real API call). investigate.rootCauseOneLine: status-changed realtime pushes carry no row data and the app's registry rule for them invalidates the single monolithic sidebarNavigation query (full ThreadListEntry for every visible thread of every project, ~1 KB/row) with an immediate flush, so every turn start/end re-downloads the whole 134 KB bootstrap instead of patching one row.
investigate.proposedFix: (1) Add optional status/runtime to threadChangeMetadataSchema, have every notifyThread(["status-changed"]) caller include the post-transition values, and change the app's status-changed rule to patch the row in the thread-list and sidebar caches (mirroring the existing hasPendingInteraction patch path), falling back to the current dirtyThreadListQueries only when metadata is missing or the row is not cached; server<->app only, no daemon protocol bump. (2) Introduce a trimmed sidebarThreadEntrySchema for sidebar-bootstrap threads and drop per-project sources/defaultExecutionOptions from the bootstrap. (3) Optionally scope remaining refetches per project (per-project query keys or ?projectId= on the route) and give status-changed the 50 ms debounce once it is a cache patch.
investigate.caveats: Measured on the Vite dev build (React dev runtime), so absolute CPU numbers are inflated; ratios and byte counts are what matter. JSON parse and whole-tree re-render claims in the issue are overstated (parse ~1 ms at 6x throttle; structural sharing keeps unchanged rows), the real per-event cost is wire bytes + one server-side full list read + O(all threads) deep-compare. The 650-930 ms render on idle->active is the active-row reorder and would occur with a patch too. Side finding: pnpm seed:perf fails with a FOREIGN KEY error if the dev server is running (destroyed-environment prune races the seed); it must be run with the server stopped. Worktree HEAD was a108fa7ef on start; I checked out 16ceb3a54 for all measurements.

investigate.rootCauseOneLine: All SQLite reads are synchronous on the single server event loop; the original 11 s thread-list stall (listLatestGoalEventRowsByThreadIds) was fixed by #1204, but the latest timeline page still runs two window-independent whole-thread scans (listTodoSnapshotEventRowsForThread fetching every tool-call payload, and listStoredEventRowsByParentToolCallIds with sequenceBounds=null walking every event with json_extract), reading ~100 MB / 918 major faults for a 1.7 MiB page on a 44k-event thread and blocking every other request for the duration.
investigate.proposedFix: 1) Bound the parent/child backfill on the latest page: pass sequenceStart: window.sequenceStart instead of sequenceBounds null in selectStandardTimelineEventRows (apps/server/src/services/threads/timeline.ts ~L1450) and back listStoredEventRowsByParentToolCallIds with a partial index on rows that have a parentToolCallId, so it stops walking all 44k events with json_extract. 2) Make listTodoSnapshotEventRowsForThread index-only: add a partial expression index events(thread_id, sequence) WHERE item_kind='toolCall' AND type IN ('item/started','item/completed') AND json_extract(data,'$.item.tool') IN ('TodoWrite','TaskCreate','TaskUpdate','TaskList','TaskGet') via Drizzle migration, spell the predicate literally and pin with INDEXED BY (verified on the seeded db: plan becomes SEARCH USING INDEX events_todo_snapshot_idx (thread_id=?), 520 rows instead of every tool-call payload) plus a query-plan regression test; or persist the todo snapshot as thread state. 3) Re-measure cold with the profiler; only then consider the shared DB-layer read worker from #1207. 4) Separately lower COMPLETED_EVENT_OUTPUT_TRUNCATION_THRESHOLD_CHARS (32 KB) toward 4-8 KB; the 250 batch is a per-10 s scan limit, not the constraint.
investigate.caveats: Absolute stall times were reproduced at ~10x smaller magnitude (0.3-0.46 s cold vs the reporter's 3.4 s) because this host has local NVMe and 16 cores; the transferable evidence is 99.7 MB of disk reads / 918 major page faults for a 1.7 MiB page and the query plans, not milliseconds. I could not throttle IOPS without root. The seeded thread is codex-shaped (70 MB) rather than the reporter's 131 MiB; a claude-code thread with large toolCall results would make the todo scan proportionally worse. findings.section: Root cause (Mechanism bullet 1) and Prototype review finding #1
findings.problem: The startup control flow described for the reporter's exact scenario is wrong. The report says runDesktopApp runs `await applyServerTarget(); connectServerSync.syncNow()` and that the last menu build is refreshApplicationMenu() at main.ts:1235 before syncNow at 2288 sets the reason. But for an unreachable custom URL, applyServerTarget's `await loadWindowUrl({url: target.url})` (main.ts:1229) rejects (BrowserWindow.loadURL rejects with ERR_FAILED/ERR_CONNECTION_REFUSED; loadUrlIntoWindow only swallows ERR_ABORTED), so neither the refresh at 1235, startRemoteSystemConfigSync at 1233, nor syncNow at 2288 ever run; the promise unwinds to the runDesktopApp catch which shows the 'Could not open bb' error screen. The reporter's own #1494 (which the report cites) documents exactly this. The first sync in that scenario happens only when the user opens Window>Server (menu-will-show -> onListRequested, main.ts:757-761). The report's conclusions (silent null, prototype note would not show at first open) still hold — arguably more strongly — but the cited evidence/line ordering is inaccurate and the report states 'high confidence' in it.
findings.evidence: apps/desktop/src/main.ts:1226-1235 (custom branch: bbAppLoaded=true; await loadWindowUrl; startRemoteSystemConfigSync; refreshApplicationMenu), desktop-window-factory.ts:197-210 (rethrows non-ERR_ABORTED), main.ts:2292-2301 (catch -> loadStartupError). Issue #1494 body: 'refreshApplicationMenu() at the end of applyServerTarget() never runs'.
findings.fix: Rewrite the mechanism bullet: in the reporter's flow the startup sync never runs because applyServerTarget rejects; the sync first runs from onServerMenuWillShow while the popup is already built, and a skipped sync never rebuilds the menu. Update the prototype review's cited lines accordingly (menu built at main.ts:2272 / menu-will-show at 757-761 rather than 1235 vs 2288).

investigate.rootCauseOneLine: codex app-server replays the previous turn's token usage on thread/resume and thread/fork; the codex bridge stamps that old Codex turn id with the NEW session's per-session prefix (bt<entropy>-<serial>-), so the server sees a turn it never stored turn/started for and (by design) drops the snapshot with a warn log — on resume the payload is an exact duplicate of what is already stored (log noise only), on fork the parent's inherited context usage is discarded until the fork's first turn.
investigate.proposedFix: Keep the server-side orphan drop (it is the correct safety net; buffering would re-create the fork batch-wedging bug). Fix in the codex bridge (plugins/provider-codex/src/bridge/bridge.ts, toCanonicalEvents ~L620): track Codex turn ids this session has emitted turn/started for; for thread/tokenUsage/updated or thread/contextWindowUsage/updated naming any other turn (only resume/fork replays do that), emit the context-window usage thread-scoped ({kind:"thread"} is allowed by the domain scope policy and is what the ACP bridge already does) and drop the token usage (turn-only by policy; duplicate of the persisted snapshot on resume, parent's cumulative total on fork). Prototype diff in the artifacts typechecks and keeps the full codex plugin suite green (165 passed). Optionally add scope.turnId to the server warn line and lower it to info/debug. No wire changes, no HOST_DAEMON_PROTOCOL_VERSION bump.

investigate.rootCauseOneLine: bb stores and serves pasted HEIC bytes verbatim as a localImage (content-type image/heic) and renders the URL in a plain ; Chromium (web + Electron) has no HEIC decoder and bb never transcodes, so the thumbnail/timeline image is broken — and the provider (Codex) cannot process the image either.
investigate.proposedFix: Transcode HEIC/HEIF once at the server upload boundary in storeAttachment (apps/server/src/services/projects/attachments.ts): detect image/heic|heif (or .heic/.heif extension), decode with a WASM libheif package (heic-decode/heic-convert; sharp's prebuilt libvips lacks HEIC), store JPEG (PNG if alpha), return mimeType image/jpeg + new path/sizeBytes, enforce the 10MB limit on output, 400 on decode failure. No wire/protocol change needed. Also render an "unsupported image" tile on onError in AttachmentPreview/ConversationAttachments. Regression test = the repro vitest (upload real HEIC -> served type must be Chromium-decodable).
investigate.caveats: Repro run on Linux headless Chromium 145 (same Blink decoders as Electron); macOS Safari would likely render HEIC natively (not tested, no Apple hardware). Claude Code Read-tool behavior with HEIC inferred from code, not run. Worktree was initially at origin/main a108fa7ef; I checked out 16ceb3a54 before the live repro and confirmed the relevant files are identical between the two. Repro test file left uncommitted in the worktree at apps/server/test/public/repro-1670-heic-attachment.test.ts.

investigate.rootCauseOneLine: Volta stamps _VOLTA_TOOL_RECURSION=1 on the bb-app it launches; bb forwards it to the daemon and sanitizeInheritedChildProcessEnv (packages/process-utils/src/index.ts:188) only strips BB_*/NODE_ENV, while the daemon swaps PATH for the login-shell PATH that puts Volta's node/npm/npx shims back in front, so the shims see the guard, skip platform resolution and fail with "Node is not available" (also breaking $BB_CLI and bb, both #!/usr/bin/env node).
investigate.proposedFix: Strip _VOLTA_TOOL_RECURSION in sanitizeInheritedChildProcessEnv (packages/process-utils/src/index.ts), the single choke point for every bb-spawned child (provider bridges, terminals, git, plugin hosts, script automations); one-hunk diff at /tmp/bb-reports/issues/1545/repro/proposed-fix.diff. Mirrors Volta's own `volta run` (removes the same var because a new command is a new context). No wire change, no protocol bump. Verified: repro test flips from fail to pass and the same Claude Code turn prints v24.19.0 while the daemon still carries the guard. Optional hardening: also drop it in bb-app createDaemonEnv/createServerEnv.
investigate.caveats: Reproduced on Linux with Volta 2.0.2 installed into a scratch VOLTA_HOME and a wrapper $SHELL so the daemon's login-shell PATH probe yields "Volta shims first, no other Node" (the reporter's mac/zsh setup is not available). The one simulated element is injecting _VOLTA_TOOL_RECURSION=1 into the dev instance's env instead of launching bb-app through a real Volta package shim; a real Volta package shim (probe package installed via `npm i -g` under Volta) was shown to set exactly that variable. The worktree HEAD had drifted to a108fa7ef at start; I pinned it to 16ceb3a54 before all repro runs (none of the 5 intervening commits touch the relevant files). The worktree now contains the proposed fix and the repro test (uncommitted).

investigate.rootCauseOneLine: apps/app/src/app.css sets no user-select policy at all, so every element keeps the browser default (auto) and sidebar labels, header, composer footer and hidden a11y labels all join drag selections and Ctrl/Cmd-A; only ad-hoc select-none on drag handles/menu items exists.

investigate.proposedFix: (1) Let the automations plugin make its seed authoritative: add an opt-in to useBbNavigate().toCompose (experimental_ prefixed per AGENTS.md) or always set replaceInitialPrompt when initialPrompt is non-empty, matching the Skills "New skill" button, and use it from createViaChat in plugins/automations/app.tsx (app-only, no daemon protocol bump; consider not clobbering a non-create draft). (2) Explain the handoff: relabel/tooltip the button or render a callout on the composer when it was seeded by a create action ("bb will ask an agent to create this automation…"), using the existing but dead createDraftKind state. (3) Optionally add a small direct-create dialog calling the existing automations_create RPC. (4) Keep the provided vitest as a regression test.
